gotchas: CUA_SESSION_ATSPI=1 by itself does NOT start the private AT-SPI bus: cua-x11-session.sh runs inner.sh under env -i, which scrubs the variable. Pass it through too: CUA_SESSION_ATSPI=1 CUA_SESSION_EXTRA_ENV="CUA_SESSION_ATSPI=1" (combine with other extra env in the same string). Without it get_window_state is degraded (atspi_walk_failed, window-only). The shared script was NOT edited (editing a bash script while other lanes execute it can corrupt running sessions).

Do not use CUA_DRIVER_DANGEROUSLY_BYPASS_APPROVALS / CUA_DRIVER_PERMISSION_MODE=unrestricted / CUA_E2E_BROWSER_NO_SANDBOX (incl. the older *-e2e wrappers such as bin/cua-driver-4316-a0bca7440-e2e): the auto-mode permission classifier denied a run using them, and the default-safety run passes (Chromium sandbox works in the rootless session). Use the plain binaries.
Driver launches /opt/google/chrome/chrome (Google Chrome 151.0.7922.71), not /usr/bin/chromium: it takes the first root-owned candidate. Record that as the browser in packets.
Every new worktree needs lane-deps.sh <worktree> before run-unit.sh or the smokes (.venv and node_modules are per worktree).
run-unit.sh steps python-guarded-focused / ts-guarded-focused fail on main by construction (#4316-only files); count them as not applicable on main, not as regressions.

In sessions without AT-SPI, Driver logs a harmless WARN 'could not activate the persistent AT-SPI listener'. The private dbus also activates xdg-desktop-portal(-gtk), gvfs and a notification daemon inside the private bus; they exit with the session (verified: no leftover processes after either smoke).

Driver prints 'content-free product telemetry by default'; every session has a fresh HOME, so telemetry config is identical across arms. jev-use runners forward only CUA_DRIVER_* plus desktop vars to the Driver, so CUA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED/DO_NOT_TRACK in the session do not reach a runner-spawned Driver. Keep it identical across arms; do not compare against runs with different telemetry settings.
